$comment: Transcribed by hand from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFCR (AIP France, chart dated 2026-10-01): the text pages checked against the images of the pages.
Only what the chart states is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text; the reporting points, rules and notes were added by hand.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.
No circuit height or circuit side is printed on this chart, so none is recorded.

A "fr" object holds the French column of the same chart for the notes, copied as printed and never translated: a French note sits at the index of its English twin and is left empty when the twin could not be paired with certainty.

The reporting points are in French: "location" is the name printed in the French column of the chart, copied and not translated, and "purpose" is written in French; a point whose French name could not be read has no "location". Only "spoken.en" is English: the name the English phraseology says over the radio.
name: Rodez-Aveyron

source.extraction: manual, from the chart text and images
source.frenchExtraction: French column of the chart text, read by script and paired with the English sentences

service.atsHours: see NOTAM; an extension or change of the ATS hours for commercial or medical flights only is announced on request on the frequency (UTC in winter, local time minus 1 h in summer)

preferredQfuReason: preferred QFU 307, due to the IFR procedure
notes: Preferred QFU 307, due to the IFR procedure.
Heavy turbulence or windshear at the runway 13 threshold with a wind from 100 to 180 degrees above 10 kt.

Free flight (hang gliding) sites: Cassagnes, 3.42 NM from the runway 13 threshold on azimuth 289, floor 577 m (NGF), vertical limits surface to 167 ft ASFC, active every day from sunrise to sunset + 30 min, used with south or south-east winds; Balsac, 1.54 NM from the runway 13 threshold on azimuth 274, floor 580 m (NGF), vertical limits surface to 167 ft ASFC, active every day from sunrise to sunset + 30 min.
Meteorological conditions with IFR traffic, visibility on the routes: S-SA-LFCR 1600 m; W-SA-LFCR 3400 m, following the Aveyron gorges until SA; E-EA-LFCR 2200 m; N-EA-LFCR 2400 m.
Aircraft with MTOW of 5.7 t or more may not line up from taxiway C. Aircraft with MTOW of 45 t or more must make the half-turn on the turn-around areas at the runway 13 and 31 ends.
Three intermediate holding points A1, A2 and A3 exist on the taxiway; a yellow taxiway is marked between A1 and A3.

Outside ATS hours the pilot-controlled lighting is available on the TWR frequency on PPR 48 HR: 3 clicks within 5 seconds broadcast the weather data and switch on low-intensity lighting and the PAPI; 5 clicks within 5 seconds, high-intensity lighting and the PAPI; lighting and PAPI switch off after 15 minutes.
Radio failure: squawk 7600, continue in visual meteorological conditions, land at the nearest suitable aerodrome and report the arrival to the ATS unit concerned by the quickest means.
